issue.title: env: use putenv_s for LC_ALL, LANG, etc.

labels.name: bug-regression
labels.description: wrong behavior that was introduced in a previous commit (please bisect)

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
```
Problem:  ":lang messages en_US.UTF-8" no longer overrides the language
          detected from the environment (at startup).
Solution: In os_setenv, special-case "LC_ALL", "LANG", et al. to use
          putenv_s instead of uv_os_setenv.
```

fixes #11045

body: @erw7 thx. I will try, although not sure how easy it would be to compile it on Win.

@habamax If you just want to try it, you don't need to build it yourself. You can use the CI artifact from the following link:

- [64bit MINGW_64](https://ci.appveyor.com/project/neovim/neovim/builds/27485261/job/bfks6e88q59n2xp6/artifacts)
- [32bit MSVC](https://ci.appveyor.com/project/neovim/neovim/builds/27485261/job/7mv9jqmdor1e9l44/artifacts)

If you use 64bit MINGW_64, see the following  https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/9461#issuecomment-514071442.
You can also `set LC_MESSAGES=en-US` before running `nvim` as a workaround until it is fixed.

set LANG=C
as environment variable before nvim.exe

>> You can also set LC_MESSAGES=en-US before running nvim as a workaround until it is fixed.

@habamax You are using Powershell. In that case, `$env:LC_MESSAGES="en-US"` should be used.

>A working work-around is to
>set LANG=C
>as environment variable before nvim.exe

In my environment, the language is set to English without any problems regardless of the environment variables `LC_MESSAGES`, `LANGUAGE`, `LANG` and `LC_ALL`.
